biography: Douglas Soares, born and raised in the bustling favelas of Sao Paulo, didn't inherit a racing pedigree; he forged one. Unlike many Brazilian racers who start with karting, Soares's journey began with illegally modified mopeds, dodging traffic and authorities in the city's chaotic streets. This reckless abandon eventually caught the eye of a local mechanic, who saw raw talent beneath the bravado and introduced him to amateur stock car racing. His aggressive style quickly made waves in the Copa Montana series, a proving ground for Brazil's next generation of motorsport stars. While his early results were inconsistent, his undeniable speed and flashy personality have earned him a dedicated fanbase and the attention of larger racing organizations. Currently, he's focused on refining his racecraft and securing a championship in Copa Montana, hoping to catapult himself into international racing.
drivingStyle: Soares is known for his aggressive, high-risk driving style. He attacks corners with a late-braking technique, often pushing the limits of grip and occasionally overstepping them. Tire management is not his forte; he prioritizes immediate speed over long-term consistency. Under pressure, he tends to become even more aggressive, sometimes leading to costly mistakes, but also pulling off incredible overtakes when the stakes are high. He thrives in wet conditions, where his raw car control and fearless attitude give him a significant advantage.

rivalries.reason: A veteran of Copa Montana, Oliveira represents the old guard of calculated, conservative racing. Soares sees him as an obstacle to be bulldozed, while Oliveira views Soares as a reckless upstart who needs to learn respect.

Costa, a rising star known for her precision and technical mastery, clashed with Soares multiple times after he forced her off the track during a critical championship race, accusing her of blocking tactics.
Santos and Soares both came from the same neighborhood and started racing together, leading to a fierce rivalry fueled by bragging rights and the desire to prove who is the better driver.

quirks: Always wears the same lucky pair of socks given to him by his grandmother before every race.
Listens to a specific samba song on repeat in the hours leading up to a race to get pumped up.
Refuses to start a race without tapping the roof of his car three times, a ritual he claims brings him good fortune.
famousQuote: "Fear? Fear is for those who watch from the stands. I'm here to drive, to win, to make them remember my name."
careerHighlight: Winning the 2022 Interlagos Copa Montana race after starting from the back of the grid due to a qualifying penalty, a masterful display of overtaking skill in treacherous wet conditions.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead on the final lap of the 2023 Copa Montana championship decider, handing the title to his rival, Ricardo Oliveira, and costing his team a substantial bonus.
